blueprint.executiveSummary: Paraag Marathe & John Lynch hold $35.16M in gross 2026 cap space ($35.16M effective after absorbing DeForest Buckner's $7.90M cap charge from ~$41.26M pre-trade space), while 2027 currently projects at -$31.54M over an estimated $327M cap ceiling. Rather than taking on multi-year veteran guarantees in-season, SF's model relies on rolling $27M–$32M of unused 2026 cap space 1-for-1 into 2027 under CBA Article 13 to neutralize that 2027 deficit and absorb scheduled option proration jumps on Brock Purdy, Nick Bosa, Fred Warner, and Trent Williams.

strategicPillars.title: 1. CBA Article 13 Rollover Bridge ($27M–$32M Target vs. -$31.54M 2027 Projection)
strategicPillars.detail: Unused 2026 cap space carries over dollar-for-dollar into 2027. Preserving $27M+ of 2026 room nearly erases San Francisco's projected -$31.54M 2027 deficit without forcing premature void-year restructures on aging veterans.

strategicPillars.title: 2. Expiring Rental Purchasing Power & Option-Bonus Architecture
strategicPillars.detail: Leading the NFC with $35.16M in 2026 cap space lets SF absorb 9/18ths prorated base salaries on expiring 1-year trade rentals ($0 2027 liability) to keep pick costs to Day 3, while Purdy ($7.55M option proration) and Bosa ($8.85M option proration) trigger April 1 spring exercises.

strategicPillars.title: 3. Rookie-Scale Trench Pipeline & Protecting 2027 Day 1–2 Picks
strategicPillars.detail: With SF's 2027 4th-round pick traded for DeForest Buckner (6 picks left: Rd 1, 2, 3, 5, 6-BAL, 7-KC), protecting Round 1–3 capital alongside 2025–2026 draftees (Mykel Williams, Upton Stout, Omar Cooper Jr., Keionte Scott, Romello Height, plus Alfred Collins returning in 2027 from season-ending IR) is mandatory against 2027 cap tightness.
